stories.title: Jaishankar's 'serial practitioner of terrorism' attack on Pakistan at UNGA81
stories.body: delivering India's national statement at the 81st UNGA general debate on 26 Sept, EAM S. Jaishankar said "yesterday, a serial practitioner of terrorism misrepresented facts before this Assembly. Arguments were invoked to normalise terrorism and claim immunity from its consequences. That will not stand." He asserted India's right to defend itself against terrorism "will be exercised", that "friendship and goodwill cannot co-exist with terrorism", and reaffirmed zero tolerance — the financial aspects of terrorism "should be exposed and countered". The remarks followed Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif's address a day earlier, where Sharif credited US President Donald Trump with a "timely intervention" in the May 2025 four-day confrontation and criticised India over the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty; India had exercised its right of reply through diplomat Petal Gehlot.

stories.title: Trump–Xi White House summit ends with no breakthrough
stories.body: US President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping on 24 Sept (Xi's first US visit in over a decade): warmer tone but no breakthroughs on Taiwan, AI, tariffs or the Iran war. The two sides agreed to a two-month extension of the US–China trade truce to 10 January 2027 (it was due to expire in November), continue work on a Board of Trade for limited goods, and hold further talks on AI — Xi said AI must be "always under human control" and invoked the Thucydides Trap (competition, not confrontation). Rare-earth/magnet supply commitments, soybean purchases and the 200-Boeing-aircraft deal stayed unresolved; the only headline "gift" was two giant pandas for Atlanta Zoo.

stories.title: Macron renews push to regulate UNSC veto at UNGA81
stories.body: French President Emmanuel Macron renewed the French-Mexican Initiative (floated 2013, launched 2015) calling on the P5 to voluntarily refrain from using the veto in cases of genocide, crimes against humanity and large-scale war crimes. Backing has reached 128 UN Member States (21 joined in mid-2026) — the first time two permanent members (France and the UK) formally committed. The veto is not named in the UN Charter — it flows from Article 27(3) (affirmative vote of 9 including concurring P5 votes); related mechanisms: the Liechtenstein Initiative (UNGA Resolution 76/262, 2022) forcing a UNGA meeting within 10 working days of any veto, and the ACT Code of Conduct. Any charter amendment to abolish the veto needs two-thirds of UNGA plus ratification by two-thirds of members including all five permanent members (Article 108) — the amendment paradox.

stories.title: AFSPA extended for 6 months in parts of Manipur, Nagaland, Arunachal
stories.body: in Gazette notifications issued 25 Sept, the MHA extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 in specified areas of the three states for six months from 1 October 2026 (till 31 March 2027), following a review of law and order. In Manipur, the disturbed-area declaration covers the whole state except areas under 13 police stations in five districts (Imphal West, Imphal East, Thoubal, Bishnupur, Kakching). In Nagaland, AFSPA continues in 9 districts (Dimapur, Niuland, Chumoukedima, Mon, Kiphire, Noklak, Phek, Peren, Meluri) plus areas under 21 police stations in Kohima, Mokokchung, Longleng, Wokha and Zunheboto. In Arunachal Pradesh, it covers Tirap, Changlang and Longding districts plus Namsai, Mahadevpur and Chowkham police-station areas in Namsai. Section 3 empowers the Centre to declare a "disturbed area".

stories.title: The RUPP conundrum: Ashok Lavasa flags shell-party funding
stories.body: former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa flagged unaccounted political funding after a BBC investigation into suspicious donations to Registered Unrecognised Political Parties (RUPPs — parties registered under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, without national/state-party status). ADR figures cited: RUPP income rose 223% in FY 2022–23, while only 739 of 2,764 parties filed audited accounts; the ECI delisted 334 of 2,854 RUPPs in August 2025 for prolonged electoral inactivity (delisting ≠ statutory deregistration — a 2002 SC ruling permits deregistration only in exceptional cases); Section 13A gives conditional tax exemptions to registered parties; estimated revenue forgone through tax exemptions on political contributions: ₹11,813 crore over a decade. Reform calls: CAG-empanelled audits, statutory deregistration powers, a party-expenditure ceiling, and a unified digital financial-reporting portal.

stories.title: Delhi HC: Muslim personal-law marriage no shield from POCSO/BNS for sex with wife under 18
stories.body: the Delhi High Court ruled that a Muslim personal-law marriage does not protect a man from prosecution under the POCSO Act or the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for sexual acts with a wife below 18 years of age, and refused to quash the case — an important exam-ready junction of personal law and criminal law.

stories.title: Operation Drishti: AFMS performs 220 sight-restoring surgeries at Tangdhar
stories.body: Armed Forces Medical Services surgeons performed 220 sight-restoring surgeries during the two-day 10th Mega Eye Surgical Camp at an underground surgical centre in Tangdhar, Kupwara, along the LoC.

stories.title: Centre notifies India's first four 'Mega Ports' under the Indian Ports Act, 2025
stories.body: the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways notified Deendayal Port (Kandla), Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva), Paradip Port and Mundra Port as Mega Ports on 25 Sept (notification in force on publication), the first set under the new classification introduced by Section 73 of the Indian Ports Act, 2025. Criteria (notified July 2026): ≥150 MMT annual cargo for bulk ports or ≥7.5M TEU for container ports; the classification stays valid 5 years even if throughput later falls below threshold, then is reviewed; it does not alter statutory status — Mundra (Adani-operated) remains a "port other than a major port". Paradip is the only east-coast Mega Port.

stories.title: SWIFT payment system in focus as BRICS eyes alternatives
stories.body: the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) is a member-owned cooperative founded in 1973, HQ'd in La Hulpe, Belgium, supervised collectively by the G10 central banks — a pure secure messaging network (not a settlement bank) linking 11,000+ banking and securities organisations across 200+ countries via BIC/ISO 20022 codes. Alternatives gaining traction amid sanctions weaponisation of the dollar: CIPS (China, 2015, yuan internationalisation), SPFS (Russia, 2014), and the blockchain-based Project mBridge multi-CBDC platform.

stories.title: FSSAI moves to bar 'analogue paneer' from using the name paneer
stories.body: the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India proposed a draft amendment to the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011 to prohibit manufacture, marketing and sale of non-dairy analogue products under the name "paneer". Analogue paneer replaces milk fat/protein with vegetable oils, starches and plant proteins — 50–70% cheaper to make than real paneer — and must be sold as a dairy analogue with transparent labelling; hotels, caterers and food-delivery platforms would have to disclose its use.

stories.title: Typhoon Dujuan batters Tokyo, eastern Japan
stories.body: Japan's 25th named storm of the season (name contributed by China, means the azalea flower) dumped a record 832 mm of rain in 48 hours on Izu Oshima, with sustained winds of 130 km/h and gusts of 194 km/h; it triggered all-time high rainfall in Tokyo's Edogawa ward, disrupted Haneda/Narita flights and bullet-train services, and its interaction with Japan's stationary autumn rain front (Akisame zensen) intensified flooding.

stories.title: Asian Games 2026, Day 7: kabaddi double gold takes India to 30 medals
stories.body: on 26 Sept India completed a golden kabaddi sweep over Iran in Aichi-Nagoya: the men won 40-34 (trailing 18-17 at half-time; Arjun Deshwal's raiding and Sumit's defending turned the final) and the women edged Iran 37-34 earlier in the day. India's 9th men's and 4th women's Asian Games kabaddi golds took the Day-7 haul to 7 medals (2 gold, 3 silver, 2 bronze) and the overall tally to 30: 4 gold, 12 silver, 14 bronze. Other 26 Sept medals: Sawan Barwal — marathon silver in 2:11:37 (national record), India's first Asian Games marathon medal since 1982 (44 years); Tajinderpal Singh Toor — men's shot put silver behind Iran's Mohammadreza Tayebi's Games Record 20.81m; women's 50m rifle 3-position team (Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa K. Vinod, Ashi Chouksey) — silver; Prachi Choudhary and the Joshna Chinappa–Velavan Senthilkumar squash pair — bronze; Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh reached the squash singles finals (medals assured).

stories.title: World Tourism Day — 27 September
stories.body: the 2026 theme is "Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism" and the official global celebration is hosted by El Salvador (San Salvador). World Tourism Day has been observed since 1980 (46th edition), instituted at the 1979 UN Tourism General Assembly in Torremolinos; the date commemorates the adoption of the UN Tourism Statutes on 27 Sept 1970. India's celebration at Bharat Mandapam: tourism contributes 5.22% to GDP and supported 8.46 crore jobs in 2023-24; Domestic Tourist Visits hit 428.55 crore in 2025, Foreign Tourist Visits rose to 2.53 crore, and foreign exchange earnings from tourism reached ₹2,76,831 crore. Digital pillars: e-Visa, the Incredible India Digital Platform and NIDHI+ (National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry); flagship schemes: Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and PRASHAD. Globally, travel & tourism contributed US$10.9 trillion (~10% of GDP) and 357 million jobs in 2024.

Trump–Xi White House summit (24 Sept): no breakthrough on Taiwan/AI/tariffs/Iran war; US–China trade truce extended to 10 Jan 2027; Xi invokes the Thucydides Trap; 2 pandas for Atlanta Zoo.

UNSC veto reform: Macron renews the French-Mexican Initiative (2015) at UNGA81 — 128 states back voluntary veto restraint in mass atrocities; veto flows from Article 27(3); Liechtenstein Initiative = UNGA Resolution 76/262 (2022).

AFSPA: extended 6 months from 1 Oct 2026 in Manipur, Nagaland, Arunachal (till 31 March 2027); Manipur excludes areas under 13 police stations; Nagaland — 9 districts + 21 PS areas; Arunachal — Tirap, Changlang, Longding + 3 PS areas in Namsai.
RUPP conundrum: Section 29A, RPA 1951 (registration); RUPP income +223% FY23; ECI delisted 334 of 2,854 RUPPs (Aug 2025); Section 13A tax exemptions; ₹11,813 cr revenue forgone over a decade.
Delhi HC: Muslim personal-law marriage no shield from POCSO/BNS for sex with a wife under 18.
Operation Drishti: AFMS — 220 sight-restoring surgeries at Tangdhar, Kupwara (LoC) — 10th Mega Eye Surgical Camp.

Mega Ports (25 Sept, Indian Ports Act 2025, Section 73): Deendayal (Kandla), JNPA (Nhava Sheva), Paradip, Mundra; criteria 150 MMT bulk / 7.5M TEU container; status valid 5 years; Paradip = only east-coast Mega Port.
SWIFT: 1973, La Hulpe, Belgium; 11,000+ institutions, 200+ countries; BIC/ISO 20022; alternatives — CIPS (2015), SPFS (2014), mBridge (multi-CBDC).

FSSAI: draft amendment to the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011 — non-dairy analogue paneer banned from the name "paneer"; analogue paneer 50–70% cheaper to produce.
Typhoon Dujuan: Japan's 25th named storm, name = azalea (China); 832 mm/48h on Izu Oshima; winds 130 km/h, gusts 194 km/h.

Asian Games Day 7: kabaddi double gold vs Iran — men 40-34, women 37-34; India tally 30 = 4 gold, 12 silver, 14 bronze; Barwal marathon silver 2:11:37 NR (first since 1982); Toor shot put silver; women's 50m rifle 3P team silver; squash bronze for Chinappa–Senthilkumar.

World Tourism Day 27 Sept: theme "Digital Agenda and AI to Redesign Tourism"; host El Salvador; observed since 1980 (46th edition); date marks UN Tourism Statutes, 27 Sept 1970; India — 5.22% GDP, 8.46 cr jobs (2023-24), DTV 428.55 cr (2025), FTV 2.53 cr, forex ₹2,76,831 cr; platforms Incredible India Digital Platform, NIDHI+; schemes Swadesh Darshan 2.0, PRASHAD.
Trade: 4–5 bilateral investment treaties (BITs) to be finalised soon; France's EDF pushing its nuclear-reactor technology in India.
